items.headline: Meloni Blames Pro-Russia Hackers for Cyberattack on Minister
items.excerpt: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni blamed pro-Russian hackers for a cyberattack on her foreign minister, after a rise in hybrid disruptions from entities aligned with Vladimir Putin’s government.

items.headline: AI Safety Advocates Make Gains After $110 Million Midterm Fight
items.excerpt: Candidates who favor stricter oversight of artificial intelligence racked up wins in key congressional races, aided by a pro-regulation political funding group backed in part by Anthropic PBC at a time when Americans are increasingly uneasy over the rapidly developing technology.

items.excerpt: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Yorkville Ives & Co. partner Dan Ives and Bloomberg US equities reporter Natalia Kniazhevich examine the sharp post-election technology selloff, as investors weigh political resistance to data centers, AI spending and the outlook for Anthropic's IPO. items.headline: Russia’s Rosstat Struggles to Restore Systems After Major Cyberattack
items.excerpt: Major Russian economic reports will be delayed through at least Nov. 13 following a recent major hack on the statistics agency Rosstat.

items.headline: SoftBank, ABB Consider China Carve-Out to Salvage Robotics Deal
items.excerpt: SoftBank Group Corp. and ABB Ltd. are looking at carving out the Chinese part of a giant robotics deal as they explore ways to salvage a transaction blocked by Beijing, according to people familiar with the matter.

items.headline: Neocloud Groq Aims to Double Value to $8 Billion Amid AI Selloff
items.excerpt: A top executive at data center operator Groq has kicked off an audacious bid to double its valuation in about three months while slamming rivals in the space for being too reliant on debt markets.

items.headline: AI Selloff Exposes Data Center Boom Risks
items.excerpt: The selloff in AI stocks is adding new uncertainty to the massive buildout of data centers across the US. items.headline: S&P 500 Posts Biggest Weekly Drop Since 2025 on AI Trade Worries
items.excerpt: US stocks logged their biggest weekly loss since April 2025 on concerns over the artificial intelligence trade after Democrats swept the US midterm elections.

items.headline: Big Take: The New AI Trade Is FOGO
items.excerpt: Wall Street’s AI rout sent US and then Asian markets tumbling, raising fresh questions about the sustainability of the global AI boom and where the next opportunities lie. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.headline: Bitcoin Steadies After Record Hack Fallout, Midterm Turbulence
items.excerpt: Bitcoin settled near recent lows after a bruising selloff on Thursday swept through cryptocurrencies and other risky assets, pressured by lackluster chipmaker earnings and a Democratic sweep of Congress.

items.headline: Brookfield CEO Says Infrastructure Is Growing Fastest
items.excerpt: Brookfield Asset Management raised $25 billion in the third quarter, driven by credit and infrastructure, as the money manager positions itself as a key player funding the build-out of artificial intelligence. He speaks to Bloomberg's Dani Burger. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.excerpt: Democrat Representative from California Sam Liccardo said that congress has 'issued a lot of press releases' on issues surrounding technology, but haven't managed to push meaningful legislation over the finish line. items.excerpt: Nadia Lovell, head of global equity strategy at UBS Global Wealth Management, says data center delays could create an “air gap” for semiconductors, pressuring inventories, prices and margins. items.headline: SpaceX Embrace of Compute Deals Eases Reliance on US Contracts
items.excerpt: SpaceX’s reliance on US government-funded contracts will continue to shrink, Elon Musk said, signaling a shift in focus away from what was previously his rocket-launch company’s most important partnership.

items.headline: Google Takes Over Wyoming Data Center That Crusoe Had Pitched
items.excerpt: Alphabet Inc.’s Google has bought out Crusoe’s data center site in southeast Wyoming, opting to take on the project itself after the AI computing upstart failed to lock in customers.

items.headline: Onsemi Scraps Plan for $2 Billion Expansion in Czech Republic
items.excerpt: ON Semiconductor Corp. scrapped plans for a semiconductor expansion in the Czech Republic that was initially valued at as much as $2 billion.

items.headline: OpenAI Staffer Pleads Not Guilty to Office Bugging Charge
items.excerpt: An OpenAI engineer charged with planting a hidden recording device in one of the company’s offices pleaded not guilty in federal court.
